messages.content:
You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

content.text:
A 45-year-old woman underwent a routine chest X-ray as part of a pre-insurance examination. Refer to Figure 1, which shows a widened right-sided mediastinum. Given this finding, which of the following is the most likely diagnosis based solely on the chest X-ray findings, considering the absence of any pulmonary parenchymal abnormalities?

A) Aortic dissection
B) Right paratracheal mass
C) Azygous continuation of the inferior vena cava
D) Mediastinal lymphadenopathy
E) Thoracic aortic aneurysm
F) Pleural effusion
